carrier_name: Mutual of Omaha (United of Omaha Life Insurance Company)

must_contain: United of Omaha Life Insurance Company

extraction_notes: This is a multi-product Mutual of Omaha (underwritten by United of Omaha Life Insurance Company) Group Insurance Proposal. Each product has its own section beginning with a bold header (e.g. "BASIC TERM LIFE AND AD&D INSURANCE") and an "Alternate:" number. For Basic Term Life and AD&D specifically (found on page 2, Alternate 1.00): there is only ONE class ("Class 1: All Eligible Employees") - no multiple classes for this product. The BENEFIT SUMMARY section has a table "EMPLOYEE TERM LIFE BENEFIT AMOUNTS" with columns Benefit/Maximum Benefit/Guarantee Issue Amount/Minimum Benefit, all flat $50,000 in this case (i.e., a flat benefit, not salary multiple). EMPLOYEE AD&D benefit amount equals the term life benefit amount (stated as text, not a table). The COST SUMMARY table under "PARTICIPATION AND COST SUMMARY" lists two rows: "Employee Term Life" and "Employee AD&D", each with Number of Lives, Total Monthly Volume, Monthly Rate (formatted as "$X.XXX/$1,000"), Total Monthly Premium, and Total Annual Premium - extract the Monthly Rate value per $1,000 for each of these two rows as the flat rate for Life and AD&D respectively. Total count of rate rows to extract for this product = 2 (Employee Term Life, Employee AD&D). Contribution structure shown as "Non-Contributory" = 100% employer paid. Note: the document also contains many other products (Voluntary Term Life/AD&D - age-banded rates; Voluntary STD and LTD - age-banded/payroll-based; Voluntary Dental, Critical Illness, Hospital Indemnity, Accident, Vision - tiered rates) which should NOT be extracted under this "Basic Life and AD&D" instruction; only extract the Basic Term Life and AD&D section (Alternate 1.00) using this flat-rate schema. Watch for similarly-formatted flat-rate LTD/STD tables per $100 of payroll in other sections if a future doc requests those products - format is "$X.XXX (Per $100 of Monthly Covered Payroll)".
